Used $\tan^{-1}$ instead of $\cos^{-1}$ on the given fraction.
Rounded $28.07^{\circ}$ up because it had a decimal part, instead of rounding to the nearer degree.

options.text: The size of the angle whose tangent ratio is $2.5$.
The tangent ratio of an angle of $2.5^{\circ}$.
options.why: Reads the number inside the brackets as an angle rather than as a ratio.

options.text: The reciprocal of the tangent ratio of $2.5^{\circ}$.
options.why: Reads the index $-1$ as a reciprocal rather than as the inverse function.

options.text: The ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse for an angle of $2.5^{\circ}$.
options.why: Reads the number as an angle and names the sine ratio rather than the tangent ratio.

questions.solution_text: $\tan^{-1}(2.5)$ is read "tangent inverse of $2.5$" and gives the angle whose ratio of opposite to adjacent is $2.5$.

options.why: Used $\sin^{-1}(0.5)$ instead of $\cos^{-1}(0.5)$.
Assumed a ratio of $0.5$ must be halfway, so the angle is halfway between $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$.
Read the ratio $1$ as opposite equal to adjacent, which is the tangent condition.
Assumed the largest ratio must belong to the smallest angle.

questions.question_text: Angle $\alpha$ has $\sin\alpha=0.3$ and angle $\beta$ has $\cos\beta=0.3$. Which angle is larger, and by how much? Work with the unrounded angles and round only the final difference, to the nearest degree.

options.why: Rounded each angle to the nearest degree before subtracting, giving $73^{\circ}-17^{\circ}=56^{\circ}$ instead of rounding the difference itself.
Subtracted correctly but assumed the angle given by a sine ratio is always the larger one, so named $\alpha$.
Made both slips: rounded $17^{\circ}$ and $73^{\circ}$ before subtracting, and named the sine angle $\alpha$ as the larger.

questions.question_text: A student solving $\tan\theta=1.5$ gets the answer $0.9828$ on a calculator. What is $\theta$, to the nearest degree?

options.why: Rounded the radian answer $0.9828$ instead of switching the calculator to degree mode.
Used $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1.5}\right)$, giving the other acute angle of the triangle.
Rounded $56.31^{\circ}$ up because it had a decimal part, instead of rounding to the nearer degree.

questions.solution_text:
The answer $0.9828$ is in radians, so the calculator is in the wrong mode.
$\theta=\tan^{-1}(1.5)$
$=56.3099\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 56^{\circ}$
